sources.title: PLACEHOLDER — Scholarly history of steppe and Silk Road foods
PLACEHOLDER — Specialist reference on Asian dumplings

short_description.text: A thin wheat dough closed around a filling and steamed, boiled or fried, made across Asia and into Europe.

concept_summary.text: The shared idea is a small parcel: a sheet of wheat dough closed around minced meat, vegetables or cheese, then cooked in steam, water or fat.
What varies from place to place is the fold, the thickness of the dough, the filling and the way the parcels are served.

origin_summary.text: Where the idea starts is not established.
Some sources link several forms to the movements of Turkic and Mongol peoples across Central Asia, while others treat the parcels of China, Anatolia and Eastern Europe as separate developments.

long_description.text: Filled wheat parcels appear in Chinese written and archaeological records earlier than in records further west.
Many accounts tie manti to pastoral peoples of the steppe, and the name turns up from Central Asia to Anatolia and the Caucasus.
In the Himalaya, momo follow the same pattern with local fillings such as yak meat or vegetables, and sources usually connect them with Tibetan and Newar cooking.
Further west, Russian pelmeni share the parcel but differ in dough, fold and filling, and their link to the eastern forms is argued rather than documented.
Because the technique needs only flour, water and a filling, parallel invention may explain part of the likeness as well as contact does.
The fillings follow what each region raises and grows, from lamb and onion on the steppe to pork and cabbage in northern China.

uncertainty_note.text: Neither the starting point nor the direction of spread is established, and some members may be independent inventions.

cultural_practice_note.text: In many places the parcels are made in large batches by several people at once, often for a festival or a family gathering.

members.explanation: The earliest well-recorded form of the parcel, boiled or steamed, and still made in quantity for the New Year.
Carried along steppe and trade routes, by several accounts; smaller parcels, often served under yoghurt.
The same parcel, pleated at the top, with Himalayan fillings and a chilli relish on the side.
Small boiled parcels with a thin dough; a link to the eastern forms is proposed but not documented.
